content: Several papers address adversarial attacks on NLP systems. Changes to text, whether word- or character-level, are all perceptible, raising some questions about what should rightly be considered an adversarial example BIBREF8 , BIBREF9 . BIBREF10 address the reading comprehension task, showing that by appending distractor sentences to the end of stories from the SQuAD dataset BIBREF11 , they could cause models to output incorrect answers. Inspired by this work, BIBREF12 demonstrate an attack that breaks entailment systems by replacing a single word with either a synonym or its hypernym. Recently, BIBREF13 investigated the problem of producing natural-seeming adversarial examples, noting that adversarial examples in NLP are often ungrammatical BIBREF14 .
